name: Comgrow Z1 20W
tagline: 20W Budget Comgrow diode: often bundled with 3D printer deals
tldr: Comgrow Z1 20W is the 20W SKU on the Comgrow comgrow z1 line. Comgrow's Z1 targets entry-level buyers, often sold alongside Ender 3D printers. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

priceRange.note: 20W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Shortest times of the Z1 line in our benchmark: ~12–18 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo, ~6–10 min for a 3 mm basswood square
Basswood up to 8 mm in our profile, against thin stock only on the lower tiers
Fill speeds of 50–120 mm/s, several times the 10W's
cons: Comgrow's own Z1 manual lists modules up to 10W only: confirm the optical rating and seller of any '20W' Z1 listing
Widest spot of the line (~0.10 mm): less suited to very fine photo detail
More smoke on an open frame: air assist and exhaust become necessary for clean cuts
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Comgrow Z1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

editorialDepth.advantages: Comgrow Z1 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: Does Comgrow officially make a 20W Z1?
faq.answer: Comgrow's Z1 manual documents 1.6W, 5W and 10W laser options. 20W Z1 listings appear mainly through marketplace sellers (sometimes as 'Z1 Pro'), so check that the listing states optical output, not electrical input, and who handles warranty.

faq.question: How thick does the Z1 20W cut?
faq.answer: Our profile lists basswood up to 8 mm, with several passes near that limit, and our benchmark cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in ~6–10 min at 3–8 mm/s. There is no official Comgrow cutting chart for this tier.

faq.question: Is the 20W worth about $60 more than the 10W?
faq.answer: For cutting, yes: our 3 mm test square drops from ~9–15 min to ~6–10 min and the thickness limit moves from thin stock to about 8 mm. For engraving-only use, the 10W ($219–299) gives a slightly finer spot for less than the 20W's $279–379.

standoutFeatures.title: Fastest Z1 tier
standoutFeatures.body: ~12–18 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo and ~6–10 min for a 3 mm basswood square in our benchmark.

standoutFeatures.title: Cuts up to 8 mm basswood
standoutFeatures.body: The only Z1 tier in our profile that moves beyond thin stock, with air assist and multiple passes at the top of the range.
